fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Open Terrain; Street Frontage; Perimeter Fencing; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations: Providing address numbers that are clearly visible from the access road could support faster responder navigation to the property, particularly given the length of the driveway from the street. Keeping the driveway clear of parked vehicles and ensuring adequate width along its full length would support apparatus movement toward both the main building and the detached structure. Because the property has a single entry and exit point, identifying an area near the main building where emergency vehicles could turn around or stage may enhance operational effectiveness. The perimeter fencing configuration is worth reviewing to confirm that gates, if present, can be readily opened to avoid delays during a response.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Heavy Ground Vegetation; Fuel Continuity; Brushland Interface; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Limited Defensible Space; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the concentration of shrubs and ground vegetation within the immediate structure perimeter would improve defensible space and may reduce fuel continuity around the building. Where vegetation is adjacent to the structure, creating separation between plants and the building exterior could reduce direct fuel contact and support suppression operations if needed. Managing the mixed and ground-level vegetation to introduce gaps and reduce continuous fuel coverage across the surrounding terrain may further limit opportunities for fire spread toward the structure. Maintaining open terrain areas already present on the property could support firefighter access and movement during suppression operations. Prioritizing vegetation management closest to the structure and working outward would support a practical, phased approach to improving overall wildfire resilience and property preparedness over time.
